v4.9.081 - the card keeps showing what you drew on (#368)

#368 A drawing could still appear to vanish: close the big view in 3x2 and the
     card sometimes fell back to the main frame, so what had just been drawn was
     no longer on screen. One device, on its own - the app's own sync racing its
     own closing animation. Nobody else needed.

     The close zooms shut over about a fifth of a second and only then decides
     "leave the card showing this version". It made that change by reaching into
     the map it had picked up when the close STARTED and altering it in place.
     Anything that replaces that map in between - a sync rebuilding the project,
     among others - left the write landing on a copy nothing reads.

     It now goes through the store. That cannot be raced, and it removes the
     whole class rather than this one instance.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, after four wrong answers

Every one of the four was reasoned rather than measured, and each cost a run:

  - "the close writes into a stale copy, so read the state fresh" - cured one
    test, broke the other
  - "then leave it as it was" - cured the other, broke the first
  - "the rebuild moves the card" - the app was made to say so, and it never once
    did, either way round
  - "the person changed it while the rebuild was in flight, so take what is on
    screen at the last instant" - the app was made to print both numbers, and at
    that instant the card was ALREADY back on the main frame

Only then did the shape become obvious: nothing moves the card, so the value is
never really put there. Traced, then fixed.

The test that catches it watches the card seven times a second and keeps the
app's own log from the instant it flips. Six failures in a row before, green
after.

ALSO

#366 - touch a device and it catches up - is written and still NOT switched on.
It fixes a setup appearing lost on a device that has been sitting behind another
window, and makes that test pass in twenty-two seconds instead of failing after
ninety. But with it on, another test fails every single time and passes every
time without it: two devices, one in a shooting order, and the desktop never
takes the tablet's writing. Asking the instant a device is touched somehow makes
it slower to hear, which is the opposite of the intent and is not understood.
Runs 1, 15, 16 and 17 fail; runs 2, 14 and 18 pass without it.

The setups test is left in the file, skipped, as the thing #366 is for.

A note on the local test server: it crashed mid-suite four times today with an
empty error. The crash is inside wrangler's own dev plumbing - the wrapper that
only exists on a laptop - not in our worker, and upgrading it to 4.125 did not
help. Nothing that runs on Cloudflare goes near it. Run 18 was clean.

27 of 28 pass; the one skipped is #366's.
